issues.title: new_click method missing must_use attribute
issues.description: The new_click method returns a TrayIconEvent that represents an important event which should not be ignored. Factory methods that create event objects should be marked with #[must_use] to prevent accidentally creating an event without handling it, which could lead to silent logic errors.
issues.rule_name: Functions Returning Values Should Be Marked with must_use Where Appropriate

issues.title: Inverted mouse button state mapping in tray icon event conversion
issues.description: The From implementation for converting tray_icon::MouseButtonState to MouseButtonState has the Up and Down states inverted. When a mouse button is released (Up) from the underlying tray_icon library, it's incorrectly mapped to Down in the Tauri TrayIconEvent, and vice versa. This will cause all tray icon click handlers to receive the opposite button state than what actually occurred, breaking event handling logic that depends on distinguishing between button press and release events. The new_click factory method added in this PR uses MouseButtonState::default() which is Up, but when real events are converted through this From implementation, the states will be backwards.

issues.title: PatternJavascript struct gated behind isolation feature breaks brownfield pattern
issues.description: The PatternJavascript struct was moved behind a #[cfg(feature = "isolation")] gate, but this struct is used in webview initialization code (manager/webview.rs line 131) for all pattern types including Pattern::Brownfield. When the isolation feature is disabled, the PatternJavascript struct won't be defined, causing a compilation error in webview.rs when it tries to instantiate PatternJavascript for brownfield applications. This change in the derive attribute placement breaks the fundamental pattern system for non-isolation builds, preventing any Tauri application that doesn't use the isolation pattern from compiling.

issues.title: Config schema/source changed without corresponding generated artifacts update
issues.description: This PR modifies `crates/tauri-utils/src/config.rs` (a source file explicitly called out by Rule 14 as driving generated artifacts such as schemas). The diff does not include any updates to the corresponding generated outputs (e.g., regenerated JSON schemas / other generated artifacts that depend on this config). Under Rule 14, changes to this file require regenerating and committing the generated files to keep them in sync.
issues.rule_name: Generated Files Must Be Kept in Sync with Source Code

issues.title: v1 config schema/source changed without corresponding generated artifacts update
issues.description: This PR also modifies `crates/tauri-utils/src/config_v1/mod.rs`, which is part of configuration/schema definitions. The diff does not include any regenerated artifacts that would normally need updating when configuration schema-related code changes (as required by Rule 14).
issues.rule_name: Generated Files Must Be Kept in Sync with Source Code

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14395 - chore: fix new clippy warnings (derive default)

structured_output.summary:
This PR is meant to fix clippy's `derivable_impls` lint. In about 15 enums across `tauri-utils`, `tauri-runtime`, `tauri-cli` and `tauri`, it replaces hand-written `impl Default` blocks with `#[derive(Default)]` and a `#[default]` attribute on a variant. It also collapses the two `cfg`-gated `MissingBundleTypeVar` variants in the bundler into one variant whose error message is chosen with `cfg_attr`. Those mechanical changes are correct: every `#[default]` sits on the same variant the old `impl` returned.

But the PR also contains three changes that have nothing to do with the lint, and each one is a bug:
- In `crates/tauri/src/tray/mod.rs`, the `From<tray_icon::MouseButtonState>` conversion now maps `Up` to `Down` and `Down` to `Up`, so every tray click event reports the wrong button state.
- Deleting the `impl Default for IsolationSide` block left its `#[cfg(feature = "isolation")]` line behind, and that line now applies to `PatternJavascript`. `manager/webview.rs` uses that struct unconditionally, so a default-feature build of `tauri` (no `isolation`) won't compile.
- The new public `TrayIconEvent::new_click` builds `Rect` from `PhysicalPosition`/`PhysicalSize` literals, but `Rect`'s fields are the `dpi::Position`/`dpi::Size` enums, so it won't type-check. It also adds public API to what is supposed to be a lint-only PR.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The derive changes are fine, but the PR breaks the default-feature build of `tauri` (orphaned `cfg`), adds a public helper that won't type-check, and reverses tray button-state reporting at runtime. All three need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
Many Tauri config and runtime enums had hand-written `impl Default` blocks that return a constant variant. Newer clippy flags these as `derivable_impls`. This PR switches them to `#[derive(Default)]` with `#[default]` on a variant. The enums cover config (`BundleTarget`, `NsisCompression`, `NSISInstallerMode`, `PatternKind`, `WindowsUpdateInstallMode`, `TitleBarStyle`), runtime (`DeviceEventFilter`), isolation (`IsolationSide`) and tray (`MouseButtonState`, `MouseButton`). Because the same variants are chosen, the observable behaviour of `Default::default()` stays the same.

The PR also touches places outside that pattern. The bundler's `MissingBundleTypeVar` error now picks its message per platform with `cfg_attr`. The tray module's conversion from `tray_icon` events, which feeds the `TrayIconEvent` delivered to app listeners, now has its `MouseButtonState` mapping changed. And `TrayIconEvent` gains a public `new_click` constructor.
steps: Start with `crates/tauri-utils/src/config.rs` and `config_v1/mod.rs`: each removed `impl Default` becomes a derive plus `#[default]` on the same variant.
Check the same pattern in `tauri-runtime/src/lib.rs` (`DeviceEventFilter`), `tauri-cli/src/interface/rust.rs`, `tauri-utils/src/html.rs` and `tauri-utils/src/lib.rs`.

Look at `crates/tauri/src/pattern.rs`: deleting the `IsolationSide` Default impl changes which item the leftover `#[cfg(feature = "isolation")]` applies to, and that item is the `PatternJavascript` struct used by `manager/webview.rs`.
Look at `crates/tauri/src/tray/mod.rs`: the `From<tray_icon::MouseButtonState>` conversion turns OS tray events into the `TrayIconEvent::Click` that app handlers receive.
Last, `TrayIconEvent::new_click` is a new public constructor built from `Rect`, whose fields come from `tauri-runtime/src/dpi.rs`.
`tauri-bundler/src/error.rs` uses `cfg_attr` to choose the error message per platform on a single variant, which the Linux and Windows util modules return.

findings.title: Leftover `#[cfg(feature = "isolation")]` now hides `PatternJavascript`, breaking non-isolation builds
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/pattern.rs`, around line 78, a leftover `#[cfg(feature = "isolation")]` attribute (it used to belong to the removed `impl Default for IsolationSide`) now gates `struct PatternJavascript`. `crates/tauri/src/manager/webview.rs` uses `PatternJavascript` unconditionally, so builds without the `isolation` feature fail. Remove that stray `#[cfg(feature = "isolation")]` line so `PatternJavascript` is always compiled, as it was before this PR. Then check with `cargo check -p tauri` using default features (no isolation).

findings.title: `MouseButtonState` conversion swaps Up and Down
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/tray/mod.rs`, lines 31-38, `impl From<tray_icon::MouseButtonState> for MouseButtonState` maps `Up` to `Down` and `Down` to `Up`. Restore the identity mapping (`Up` to `Up`, `Down` to `Down`). Then add a unit test in the existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in the same file that converts both `tray_icon::MouseButtonState::Up` and `::Down` and asserts the results, so a future swap is caught.

findings.title: `TrayIconEvent::new_click` builds `Rect` with the wrong field types and adds public API to a lint PR
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/tray/mod.rs`, lines 137-154, the new public `TrayIconEvent::new_click` constructs `Rect { position: PhysicalPosition {..}, size: crate::PhysicalSize {..} }`. But `Rect`'s fields are `dpi::Position` and `dpi::Size` enums (see `crates/tauri-runtime/src/dpi.rs`), so it doesn't type-check. This PR is a clippy-only cleanup, so the preferred fix is to delete `new_click` entirely. If it must stay, build the event with `Rect::default()` and `PhysicalPosition::default()`, add a `.changes` file for the new public API, and add a test.

findings.title: Derive conversions keep the same default variants
findings.body:
I checked every `#[derive(Default)]` + `#[default]` conversion against the removed `impl Default`. Each one keeps the original variant: `BundleTarget::All`, `NsisCompression::Lzma`, `NSISInstallerMode::CurrentUser`, `PatternKind::Brownfield`, `WindowsUpdateInstallMode::Passive`, `TitleBarStyle::Visible`, `DeviceEventFilter::Unfocused`, `IsolationSide::Original`, `MouseButtonState::Up` and `MouseButton::Left`. `#[default]` on a unit variant of a `#[non_exhaustive]` enum (`TitleBarStyle`) and of serde tagged enums (`PatternKind`, `DeviceEventFilter`) works fine, so serialization and config defaults are unchanged.

The bundler change, which uses `cfg_attr` to choose the `#[error]` message on a single `MissingBundleTypeVar` variant, is also correct. It's a tidier replacement for the duplicate `cfg`-gated variants and works for both the Linux and Windows util callers.
